1:2.p: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.

1:12.p: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

2:9.p: So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.

2:20.p: Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labour which I took under the sun.

3:9.p: What profit hath he that worketh in that wherein he laboureth?

3:10.p: I have seen the travail, which God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.

3:13.p: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it is the gift of God.

4:2.p: Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.

4:6.p: Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.

4:7.p: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.

4:11.p: Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?

5:5.p: Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.

9:17.p: The words of wise men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.

10:7.p: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.

11:4.p: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.
